title: The two-source unitary orbital integral
statement: Evaluate \(\int_{U(N)}\exp\sum_{\mu=1}^2\operatorname{Tr}(U^*P_\mu UQ_\mu)\,dU\) for diagonal source matrices, specifying whether the target is a convergent series, a compact finite formula or large-\(N\) information.
status: As of 12 November 2026, the general integral has exact convergent Haar expansions; an explicit rank-two formula and rank-three expansions appear in \citet{holguin2024multimatrix}. The chapter develops a checked finite-rank formula and controlled series. No general compact HCIZ-type determinant or general large-\(N\) solution is claimed.

title: Riemann hypothesis in the toroidal and horocycle formulations
statement: Do all nontrivial zeros of \(\zeta(s)\) satisfy \(\operatorname{Re}s=1/2\)? In the recorded approach, can toroidal spectral parameters be put in a suitable positive unitary realization, or equivalently can the requisite RH-strength horocycle remainders be proved under the stated test-function hypotheses?
status: Open as of 12 November 2026. The toroidal structure theorems and qualitative horocycle equidistribution are established, but the positivity and zero-location conclusions are not.

title: Orientable gluings of a labelled polygon by genus
statement: For a labelled oriented \(2n\)-gon, count orientation-reversing pairings of its sides whose quotient has genus \(g\), with cyclic rotations kept distinct.
status: Solved before the recorded discussions by Harer and Zagier (1986), with an exact coefficient formula, a recurrence, and a Gaussian-matrix derivation. As of 12 November 2026 this is an established enumeration theorem.

title: Coloured planar maps with controlled face counts and interfaces
statement: Enumerate rooted orientable planar maps with specified numbers of faces of the prescribed degrees and colours, and a specified number of edges between unlike colours; specify primal/dual and rooting conventions before extracting coefficients.
status: As of 12 November 2026, formal multi-matrix generating functions and the planar Ising solution provide the recorded framework. The notebook does not select a unique finer counting convention, so no unsolved numerical problem is inferred.

title: Artin holomorphy for nontrivial irreducible complex representations
statement: For every nontrivial irreducible continuous finite-dimensional complex representation \(\rho\) of the absolute Galois group of a number field, is its Artin L-function entire?
status: Open in general as of 12 November 2026; Brauer induction proves meromorphic continuation, and abelian, monomial and numerous other cases are known. Recent partial holomorphy criteria do not establish the universal conjecture.

title: The normalized mean-field spin-glass ground energy
statement: Determine the deterministic limit of \(N^{-1}\min_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^N}N^{-1/2}\sum_{i<j}J_{ij}\sigma_i\sigma_j\) for independent standard Gaussian couplings.
status: Solved in the variational sense as of 12 November 2026 by the zero-temperature Parisi formula of Auffinger and Chen (2016 preprint; 2017 publication). This is a mean-field theorem, with the normalization and Gaussian assumptions explicit.

title: Parisi ultrametricity of asymptotic spin-glass overlaps
statement: Identify a rigorous thermodynamic interpretation of the hierarchical overlap assertion and prove ultrametricity of the resulting replica array.
status: As of 12 November 2026, Panchenko\textquoteright s theorem proves ultrametricity for random overlap measures satisfying the Ghirlanda--Guerra identities (2011 preprint; 2013 publication). It does not assert ultrametricity for arbitrary finite near-ground-state sets.

title: Explicit integral and de Rham comparison for Chern classes
statement: Construct explicit Cech/de Rham comparison data, preferably through low-weight motivic complexes, for the integral Chern classes of a holomorphic vector bundle.
status: As of 12 November 2026, functorial Deligne Chern classes exist, and inspected explicit weight-two formulas construct the comparison through the Bloch complex and dilogarithm. The announced 1987 paper is bibliographically identified, but its complete higher-weight formulas were not inspected. This access limitation is not classified as mathematical openness.

title: Beilinson--Soule motivic vanishing
statement: For every field \(F\), positive weight \(p\), and \(j\le0\), prove \(H^j(F,\mathbb Q(p))=0\); compare with the stronger integral sheaf-amplitude requirement \([1,p]\) stated in the notebook.
status: Open in general as of 12 November 2026. Modern motivic complexes exist, the upper-degree comparison with Milnor K-theory is established, and important arithmetic cases are known. Garkusha\textquoteright s criteria and Soul\'e\textquoteright s 4 November 2026 interview explicitly retain the general lower-degree conjecture.
